# s305 — Sibling id refusal ignores case

`add --id` refuses an explicit id that a sibling worktree filed under a different case (ours `S10`, theirs `s10`), and `check` warns about the pair, because on a case-insensitive filesystem the two slice files are one file after the merge.

**Findings:** s301 relay review, 2026-10-15: a sibling's s10 against our S10 is not refused; Index.get is case-sensitive · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-16** — Ready for review: explicit sibling ids are compared without case; case-only matches refuse with case_collision before writing, while inherited ids retain existing behavior. Check warns for case-only pairs even when titles match. Added three regression tests, updated error-code documentation, changelog and architecture. Verified 39 sibling tests; full suite 2322 tests in 1519.372s, OK (1 skipped); four mutations killed; documentation-selected test, slicer check and diff check passed. **Not in this slice:** the add-time cost of the sibling lookup (about 6 git calls per explicit add; a separate later note on s301); `migrate --force` and legacy ids; case handling for allocated ids (they are always lowercase, so they cannot clash by case).

## Why

s301 (landed 2026-10-15) made `add --id` refuse an id that a sibling worktree filed on its own (`ops._refuse_id_taken_elsewhere`, `src/slicer/ops.py:326`). Its review found that the lookup is exact: `sibling.get(item_id)` compares ids with `==` (`Index.get`, `src/slicer/model.py:659`), so a sibling's `s10` does not stop our `add --id S10`. Inside one checkout, `ids._refuse_case_clash` (`src/slicer/ids.py:79`) already refuses an id that differs from an existing one only in case, with the code `case_collision`, because the two are one file on a case-insensitive filesystem. Across worktrees nothing does: the merge brings `s10.json` and `S10.json` together, which is the same clash. `check._sibling_collisions` (`src/slicer/check.py:68`) matches on the exact id too, so it says nothing either.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ops.py`, `_refuse_id_taken_elsewhere`: find the sibling item by case-folded id, as `_refuse_case_clash` compares. An exact match keeps today's `id_taken_elsewhere`. A match that differs only in case is refused with `case_collision`, and the message names the worktree, their id and their title, and suggests `slicer next-id`. An id both checkouts inherited (in either case) is left alone, as today. Nothing is written.
- `src/slicer/check.py`, `_sibling_collisions`: also warn when a sibling's new id equals one of ours only after case-folding. The warning names both ids and the worktree and says the slice files will be one file on a case-insensitive filesystem.
- `docs/agents.md` (`case_collision` now also covers a sibling worktree), `CHANGELOG.md` under Fixed.
- `tests/test_sibling_ids.py`, beside the s301 tests (use the same fixtures).

- `test_Add_ExplicitIdCaseFoldOfInheritedId_Unchanged`: an id both inherited behaves as today.
